title: Priority Pulse: Resilience Heatmap + Handoff Log (week of 2026-12-15)
content:
Objective:
This note captures the week-ahead / week-behind resilience priorities, a concise incident summary from Dec 14, SLO telemetry highlights, and on-call handoff items. Treat this as the single page 'what you need to know' for the SRE rotation this week.

Executive summary:
- Dec 14 spike: a concurrent connection surge to the edge LB triggered a series of transient 503s for ~22 minutes affecting ~6% of requests to hosted-api region-us-west. Root cause: mis-applied autoscale cooldown + recent proxy change (see timeline). No data loss. Customer-facing latency SLO for p95 breached for 20 minutes.
- SLO health: API request success SLO currently 99.85% (7d rolling) vs target 99.9%. Embedding pipeline remains green.
- Priority for rotation: patch runbook gaps for LB cooldown changes, add a synthetic canary for connection-churn, and roll an immediate guardrail in autoscaler to prevent simultaneous scale-down + config rollout.

Incident (Dec 14) — condensed timeline:
- 10:02 UTC: spike in concurrent connections observed on region-us-west LB telemetry (sudden +180% above typical).
- 10:04 UTC: autoscale controller initiated scale-down due to noisy metric (bug in smoothing window).
- 10:05–10:10 UTC: config rollout of proxy v2.14 started; some nodes drained while smoothing flip-flopped.
- 10:07–10:24 UTC: error budget consumption saw a jump; tenants on high-concurrency routes received 503s.
- 10:25 UTC: on-call (pager rotation 3) manually forced scale-up and paused rollout; traffic stabilized by 10:30 UTC.

Impact:
- ~22 minutes of elevated 5xx and timeouts, peaking at 6% failed requests for a 10-minute window.
- No persisted data corruption. Metrics and traces retained.
- Several PLG customers reported degraded UI generation features; CS escalations opened (JIRA-1219).

Immediate remediation taken:
- Rolled back proxy v2.14 in region-us-west and paused global rollout.
- Tweaked autoscaler smoothing window to ignore 1-minute spikes for the next 48h.
- Added temporary circuit-breaker rule to reject new ephemeral connections if node drain > 25% in 1m window.

Root-cause hypothesis (working):
1) Autoscaler smoothing logic used instantaneous connection rate for scale decisions; a short-lived external burst caused a scale-down decision.
2) The proxy v2.14 rollout introduced additional per-connection cost during drain which compounded the pressure.
3) Orchestration order allowed scale decisions and config rollouts to race; lack of guardrail permitted both to proceed.

Open investigations / follow-ups:
- IH-01: Full tracing + flame graphs for v2.14 connection handling under drain (owner: Marcus) — due 2026-12-18.
- IH-02: Autoscaler unit tests for smoothing windows and synthetic spike scenarios (owner: Linnea) — due 2026-12-17.
- IH-03: Review orchestration ordering to ensure config rollouts wait for stable capacity (owner: Diego) — due 2026-12-19.

SLO telemetry snapshot (as of 2026-12-16):
- API success SLO (99.9% target): 7d rolling = 99.85% 
- p95 latency (target < 180ms): 7d rolling = 172ms (spike to 420ms during incident window)
- Embedding pipeline throughput: 24h average within expected 98th percentile.

Risk heatmap (current):
- High: orchestration + autoscaler interactions — actionable (task: add guardrail, test harness).
- Medium: global rollouts without per-region canaries — mitigated by temporary pause but needs longer-term policy.
- Low: hardware capacity in us-west (forecast shows 8% headroom) — monitor.

On-call handoff (what you should know going into the next shift):
- Pager rotation: Week 50 (Dec 15–21): Marcus (primary), Linnea (secondary), Asha (follow-on).
- Key playbooks to review before the shift: LB-scale-troubleshoot, proxy-rollback-runbook, autoscaler-debug. Links in linked_artifacts.
- Active alerts to watch: LB-conn-spike, autoscale-errorbudget-drift, rollout-failure-rate.
- Escalation threshold: if p95 > 300ms for >15m or errors >3% for >10m escalate to ENG-Infra lead.

Runbook gaps identified (needs work this sprint):
- Missing explicit guardrail for simultaneous scale events + rollouts (add a precondition check).
- Connection-churn synthetic not present in canary suite — add a short-lived burst test that simulates ephemeral clients.
- Troubleshooting steps for transient 503s are scattered; consolidate into one quick-reference (top-5 checks).

Action items (short-term, owner, ETA):
- AF-01: Add precondition in rollout controller to detect active scale events and pause rollout (owner: Diego) — ETA 2026-12-20.
- AF-02: Implement 1m spike ignore in autoscaler config and add unit tests / canary (owner: Linnea) — ETA 2026-12-17.
- AF-03: Add a synthetic canary that injects connection churn into canary region (owner: Marcus) — ETA 2026-12-19.
- AF-04: Draft blameless postmortem outline and notify CS about customer impact summary (owner: Asha) — ETA 2026-12-17 (postmortem full due 2026-12-22).

Proposed longer-term changes (backlog):
- Orchestration transaction model: ensure config rollout and autoscale make decisions against coherent capacity snapshots.
- Expand canary suite to include resource pressure tests (CPU, connection, ephemeral bursts) per region.
- Metric-driven canary gating: only allow global rollouts if regional synthetic pass rate > 99.95% for 30m.

Meeting reminders / syncs for this week:
- Wed 09:00 UTC: SRE triage (owners present: Marcus, Linnea) — cover IH-01/IH-02 status.
- Thu 16:00 UTC: Runbook workshop — consolidate quick-reference guide.
- Fri 11:00 UTC: Postmortem readout with CS + product (Asha leading).

Notes to the next on-call:
- If you see LB conn spikes, do not trigger a global rollback immediately — first: check autoscaler smoothing and active rollout list; if both present, pause rollout and scale-up manually.
- Keep CS updates short; Asha will maintain the postmortem thread.

Questions / unresolved items to raise at the triage sync:
- Should we introduce a temporary global rollout freeze until IH-01 is closed? Pros/cons.
- Is the autoscaler smoothing window fix a configuration-only change, or do we need a code patch to prevent regression?

Appendix (quick links and data pointers):
- Live dashboards: /dashboards/slo-overview, /dashboards/lb-conn-telemetry-us-west
- JIRA: JIRA-1219 (customer escalations), JIRA-1247 (postmortem draft)
